newcomer.plan:
PLAN: "Build an old mountain monastery courtyard in Blender for a film"
(Nothing built. Everything below comes only from the plugin folder. Where I give a number I say where it comes from; "measured", "judged" and "invented" are the plugin's own words.)

0. WHAT I READ, AND WHAT I WOULD ASSUME
Read: README; make-explainer-film and house-rules.md; the whole tips guide (kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md); surfaces-wear-and-construction (SKILL, the-required-steps, construction-and-scale, surface-recipes, wear-recipes, style-rule-and-measures, fresh-checkers, rendering-on-rented-cards, batched-rounds-and-card-time, blender-5-traps, worked examples); build-and-paint-a-place; make-3d-models and its MCP notes; "07 Composing a shot"; camera-and-framing; the five place agents; the build-a-place workflow; the place-kit data (roles, place types, Poly Haven sample); the reminder hook. That request matches the hook, so the plugin's own first line is "read surfaces-wear-and-construction before anything, and if it is for the film also build-and-paint-a-place". The person did not say "plain Blender" or "no plugin", so the plugin applies in full.
Assumptions I would say out loud: (a) "for a film" means this plugin's film: a tall 1080 x 1920 phone frame, the place seen through a few planned views (`"for_film": true`); (b) the nearest place preset is `village` (stone walls, slate or shingle roofs, paving, timber doors; there is no monastery preset); (c) nothing is paid for until the person says yes to an exact cost.

1. FREE GROUNDWORK (before I ask anything)
- Run `explainer-film-setup /path/to/work/film-kit`. It checks Node 18+, Python 3.10+ with numpy, Pillow and opencv, ffmpeg, Chromium, Blender 5.2.x, Xvfb (EEVEE needs a virtual screen), and prints the "Blender 5.2 probe". I read every line. `df -h`: stop and report under about 0.4 GB free. `export EXPLAINER_FILM_BLENDER_THREADS=2` for every Blender run.
- `explainer-film-place rent status` and `rent balance` (never print or write the person's settings). This tells me whether Cycles on a rented card is possible. If not, I say so; I do not quietly fall back to EEVEE for lit scenes.
- Start the notes folder: project story, Decisions.md (the person's exact words quoted, then my own calls so they can overturn any in one line), Status.md, Lessons.md. Files given to the person get a two-digit log number and plain words.
- Open the card-time ledger with a first-round total: `explainer-film-place card-time start --team-minutes 30 --ledger LEDGER` (the house total is 60 judged; 30 is my choice for a start-small round and I tell the person). Allowances by role: builder 10 min, fixer 5, integrator 10, renderer 10, checker 3, planner 0.

2. WHAT I TELL AND ASK THE PERSON FIRST (one short message, not a menu)
Say what happens next and what it costs: nothing is paid; the only possible cost is limited rented-card time for small pictures. Say what the method cannot do: a painted plate covers one view and a little more (a slide of about 1.29 times nearer at most), so no camera that walks through the whole courtyard and no light that reacts to people moving; if they want a fly-through, that is a different, later project and I ask which sequence comes first.
Ask only what is a want or a story choice (the tips guide lists these as things only a person or critic can judge), each with my default so "yes" is enough:
 1. Which kind of monastery and age? Default: stone-walled, slate or wooden-shingle roofed, Alpine-style, a few centuries old, because I can source its sizes and inscriptions. Tibetan, Orthodox, Japanese or Ethiopian would change walls, roofs, symbols, clothes and lettering, and I would research first and have the history critic and fact checker check every symbol and every inscription (a sacred symbol can read as something else on a phone).
 2. In use or abandoned? Default "lived in" (a swept, working place). "Ruined, abandoned for years" would be look `derelict`.
 3. What does the film say happens in this courtyard (the subject), and when (time, season, weather)? Default: late afternoon, early autumn, dry, no snow; the subject is the stone well and the worn steps to the main hall door with one lit lamp left on a step.
 4. Reference pictures? (They make the style guard non-provisional.) And confirm the tall phone frame.
While waiting I only do the free tradition-neutral things in section 1.
Decisions I make myself and state: place type `village`; look `lived_in`; state `damp` (the plugin's rule: damp outdoors where there is water or deep shade, and a courtyard with a well and high walls has both); one sun lamp.

3. WHAT I WOULD MAKE (6 parts, one owner each, ground first and frozen)
A courtyard of about 22 x 16 m paved (my starting size; the planner confirms with sources), enclosed on three sides, a low parapet on the fourth with mountains beyond.
 1. ground_and_world (built first, alone, then frozen; it also makes the cameras `View wide`, `View well`, `View hall_door`, the one sun, the world and render settings, so ownership.json names it in `frozen.set_by`): cobble and flagstone paving (`ground.stone_paving`, displaced) with a drain gully and swept footfall lines gate to hall door and to the well; gravel and earth at the edges; the world round the place: rings of real-shape ridges lighter and bluer when far (role `backdrop`, unlit, no shadow), plain ground to the horizon with its edge hidden, every camera's clip end 1500 m, no haze volume (the audit's "place: world" looks for this).
 2. main_hall: thick stone walls (`wall.stone`) with deep window and door reveals, a lintel or arch, a slate or shingle roof (`roof.slate` or `roof.shingle`) with a few slipped or missing pieces built as shape, big eaves, a small bell turret or tower (skyline), worn stone steps (`stone.step`) with shallow dips built as shape, door leaves (`timber.door`), iron hinges and bands (`iron.fitting`), small glass panes (`glass.window`).
 3. cloister_gallery: a timber gallery along one side: footing stones (`stone.footing`), posts (`timber.post`), beams tenoned into post pairs (`timber.beam`), balustrade (`timber.fence`), plank floor, an outer stair. Nothing may span more than 1.38 m between supports (judged, from the garden bridge).
 4. gate_and_walls: gatehouse arch, boundary and parapet walls with coping, a wall-foot band, steps.
 5. well_and_props: well or basin (`stone.well`), bucket, a rope built as a mesh (`prop.rope`), barrels, firewood (`prop.wood`), a bench, a lantern whose glow box sits 3 cm proud of the lamp and is hidden from the lamp's own rays (a lamp inside its own glow box is blocked in Cycles), imported Poly Haven props only where they fit the era (no plastic crates), each measured after import and checked for brands and digits.
 6. trees_and_planting: one or two pines or junipers built by hand (the kit's `grow` only makes tufts, clover, nettle, fern, bramble, moss cushions and litter): flat pointed needle clumps in layers with gaps, `tree.bark`, `plant.foliage`.
Every object gets its owner and role AS IT IS MADE (`pk.new_part_object(owner, role, name, mesh)`); I read `explainer-film-place roles --list`. There is no bronze role for a bell: I tag the nearest role, say so as a gap, and do not invent a role. Wear that the pass does not make I build as shape: the drip line under the eaves, dark soft shapes under the well and at post feet, a tide-line-style stain at the basin, a rust run below an iron ring, worn dips, slipped slates, one new board among grey ones.
Any inscription (a carved date, a name board, a plaque) carries real lettering made by our own code on its own surface; the audit fails a sign without lettering. Few of them, no invented script that only looks like writing, a made-up monastery name checked so it does not copy a real one, dates and weekdays checked. Letters the page needs must be at least 20 px tall at phone size (fail under 20, warn under 25; judged).
Budgets (house numbers): at most 1,000 objects in all; thousands of slates, cobbles and tufts built in bulk into ONE mesh per material (under about 300,000 triangles before displacement), never one object at a time (the garden's leaves took 7 minutes one by one and 10 seconds in bulk, measured). Bevels: walls 8 to 15 mm, timber 6 to 12 mm; no two siblings alike.

4. THE STEPS, IN ORDER, WITH THE PLUGIN PARTS AND COMMANDS
Step 1. Plan (agent `place-planner`, through workflow `build-a-place`): style-note.md (first line PROVISIONAL unless there are references; the plugin's rule "These things need to be integrated into the style. So it's just part of design." stays word for word; the person's own words at the top; ten hex colours and ONE hot accent, for example one door colour; what the style does not have), real-world-facts.json (every size with unit, source, confidence; a remembered number is a guess until sourced; the generic wall-thickness range of 0.1 to 0.9 m is too thin for monastery walls, so I would write the place's own sourced fact), place-settings.json (`place_type: village`, look, state, `for_film: true`, the `picture` camera and 1920 px height so marks are sized in picture dots, footfall lines, keep-clear shapes at the well surround, steps and door thresholds, one `never` rule for helpers), ownership.json, acceptance.json, 12 to 16 readable features (a stranger at half size could name them: worn steps, slate roof with gaps, mossy north wall, well, lamp, gallery posts...). Two things that must be readable at a glance in the half-size picture get different colour, roof and shape (for example hall against gatehouse).
 Workflow call: `Workflow explainer-film:build-a-place` with plugin, kit, folder, the request word for word, place "monastery courtyard", `film: true`, today's date, `blenderThreads: 2`, `maxParallelBuilders: 2` (slow computer), `effort: medium`, `checkEffort: medium` if the person keeps to "medium, never higher", `finals: false`, `rented` from `rent status`, `cardTeamMinutes: 30`. Honest caveat from the README: this workflow and its agents ran only against canned helpers, never under the real Workflow tool, and it has no resume, so a second run re-plans. I would watch its first phase, verify its reports myself against the files (never trust a helper's claim), and fall back to the same steps by hand with agent types `explainer-film:place-planner`, `place-builder`, `place-integrator`, `place-renderer`, `place-checker` if it fails.
Step 2. Plan every view before anything is drawn (preflight `shots`, first run): a rough place-facts file from the planned layout (`calculators/place_facts_schema.json`, check with `place_facts.py check`); for each view `plan_shot.py --place-facts F --view V --plan`, then `frame_geometry.py slide|reach|boxes`, `view_audit.py audit`, `plan_lights.py plan`; `plan_effects.py wind` only if a chimney or incense smoke is in frame. Then `explainer-film-preflight shots --project FILM_FOLDER --place-facts F --shot-list SHOTS.json`. The ground builder gets the camera spot, eye height and turn from the planner.
Step 3. Ground part alone: `explainer-film-place combine --scene start.blend --stages stage_ground_and_world.py --owners ownership.json --save-as ground-frozen.blend`.
Step 4. Other five parts side by side (agent `place-builder`, one stage file each, `apply(options)` idempotent, built on a COPY of the frozen ground, `pk.seat_on_ground`), each running its own share: `finish-part --owner NAME --quick --save-as part.blend`, `construction`, `normals-test`, and `combine ... --order plain` (must say idempotent and no violations). Blender runs use `-t 2`.
Step 5. Combine (agent `place-integrator`): `combine --scene ground-frozen.blend --stages (the five stages) --order both --owners ownership.json --save-as combined.blend` (plain order, reverse order, run twice; a part that touched what is not its own is a violation sent back to its owner), then `finish --scene combined.blend --settings place-settings.json --facts real-world-facts.json --save-as finished.blend` (never `--quick` for a final).
Step 6. Prove it: `explainer-film-place audit --scene finished.blend --settings place-settings.json --facts real-world-facts.json --out place-audit.json`, then `explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit place-audit.json --blend finished.blend --place-settings place-settings.json --reports REPORTS`. It must PASS before I draw, render or paint anything. Read the first FAIL, fix by category (the table in the-required-steps.md step 5), rerun; at most two repair rounds before any picture; geometry faults go back to the owner, the integrator only edits settings, role tags and dials; I never lower a requirement and never sign an accepted entry for the person. Never save the scene after the audit; if I do, audit again (a stale audit is refused). Also `model_lint.py` on the scene (stripes, same-plane faces, `.001` names, glass, sizes).
Step 7. Second `shots` run: now that the scene exists, write the place facts from it (assemble script plus `make_check_file.py`, only the story roles are mine), rerun `explainer-film-preflight shots`.
Step 8. First picture only (start small): `renderer-for`, then `render --job JOB.json --where auto` of the FIRST view (the wide one) at 540 x 960; read the render log (a "Shadow buffer full" or "Could not allocate shadow atlas" line means it cannot be judged); `measure PICTURE --make-guard` (provisional), 100 percent crops of the wear and a phone-size 300 px look. STOP and show the person: before-and-after sheet, what was measured, what was judged, what I did not test, the card seconds used.
Step 9. After their reaction: the other views small, the fresh checkers, one fix round, a different fresh checker, final gate (section 7). Full-size pictures once, at the very end, only when asked.
Step 10 (only on the person's yes, with exact cost, read live): paintings and the film page route (`paint_request.py request`, preflight `plates`, `paint`, `pages`, build-cinema-page, critique, film). About 44 US cents per 2k repaint with a style picture at 4.8 cents a megapixel on 16 October 2026; I read the live price first because it doubled in a day once. Not part of this request.

5. HOW I TEST CHANGES
- Two kinds of test. Free measured checks run here and cost no card time, so one change then measure again is right there: the shot checker (`BLEND=finished.blend paper-film/tools/check-shot.sh SHOT_SCRIPT CHECK_FILE OUT`; fix problem 1 only, in order camera, then props, then light, rerun), `construction`, `normals-test` (sun from +X must read well above its flipped-green control), `audit`, `model_lint.py`, `plan_shot.py`, `frame_geometry.py`, `view_audit.py`, `plan_lights.py plan`. Looking at pictures follows the batch rule instead.
- Batch rule for pictures: write EVERY change I plan, make them in ONE sweep, save the scene once, look once. For each change I am unsure of, about 10 far-apart variations in ONE batch: `variations make` (with `--range KEY LOW HIGH` so the settings cover the part that shows), `variations scout FILE.json` (free, tiny, on this computer; it names the ones that would not show), `variations plan` (free), `variations run FILE.json --where rented --helper builder-walls --role builder --ledger LEDGER` (up to 3 cards at once, one labelled sheet with range, detail, colour shift, saturation and squint), pick or combine, at most ONE `variations refine` batch; a third is refused. Give the run a 10-minute limit; if cut off, `variations collect RUN-FOLDER`. Small quick pictures until the end.
- Which changes I would batch for this place: moss and lichen on the shaded faces (`amount.moss_and_algae`, `dials.moss_and_algae.cover`); crack and chip density on walls and paving; wear on the state (dry, damp); and, as script hooks (`variation_hook.py` template), the number of slipped slates, the depth of the dips in the steps, the lean of the gallery posts, the sun azimuth and elevation (after the free arithmetic below).
- "Unchanged" claims: at least three draws each of old and new plus a control, compared with `calculators/regression_compare.py --old OLD --new NEW`; I say how many draws. Before blaming a change for speckle, redraw the unchanged version.
- After any change to the saved scene: audit again; keep the old version beside the new under a clear name with a note on how to go back (`undo` exists); a part that got worse in a fix keeps its old version. Before a long or paid step: `explainer-film-preflight STAGE --gate`.
- Every card job is in the ledger from the moment it is sent; `card-time show` and `check`; the tool warns at 80 percent and refuses past the allowance; over only with a written reason and never by more than half again; I never message a helper that is spending money.

6. HOW I WOULD LIGHT IT
- Exactly ONE sun lamp, added BEFORE `finish` (the wear layers read it to decide which sides stay damp and mossy; with none or two they assume 135 degrees compass and 45 up). Daylight needs a sun, a sky and a softer fill from the other side so shadows are not black; `explainer-film-place light --sun-only` adds just a sun if the scene has none.
- The sun can do nothing, so I work it out first: shadow length = height / tan(elevation). A gallery eave at 5 m with the sun 35 degrees up throws 5 / 0.700 = 7.1 m of shadow; a 12 m bell tower throws 17 m, across the whole courtyard. So the tower goes on the side away from the sun, or I accept the shade and say so. My aim: most of the courtyard in cool shade with ONE warm sunlit slot landing on the well and the steps, from the side so cobbles, steps and wall relief read under raking light. That also makes the subject the brightest thing (the plugin wants it at least 1.8 times the frame's mean and warm light 1.5 to 3 percent of the frame). The audit's line "place: sun" reports the share of seen ground in shadow; over half is a LOOK, which I report and the person decides whether to accept.
- Subject's own narrow key from below (the lamp on the step) linked to the subject alone; only a few lights cast shadows (sun, lamp, sky); people would get soft foot patches, no long shadows; glowing things get a black base colour; the lamp sits above or inside, never on a wall face; a light's reach is cut before its strength. Start from `plan_lights.py plan` watts and reach, then tune by the checker's numbers, one named light per round, not by eye (the notice corner took 26 rounds by eye).
- Renderer: the film owner's rule is Cycles where any lamp, lit window, lantern or fire is on, EEVEE when they are off; the plugin adds Cycles when water is in view. My lamp and the well water therefore mean Cycles, on a rented card; `renderer-for` prints the reasons. One renderer for every plate of one place. If no card is set up I draw only tiny Cycles previews here and say they are not a fair look. Exposure target 1.0 to 1.8 per view (judged). Check the value range: under 0.5 percent of dots clipped at either end (judged).
- Draw the first preview under three lights (flat, side, and wet if the place is wet): a mark that vanishes under one is not carrying the place. Sett joints are made darker, duller and sloped, not cut as grooves (grooves looked worse).

7. HOW I WOULD FRAME IT (tall 1080 x 1920, computed before drawn)
- Camera: where a person would stand (in the gateway arch, not in the middle of the empty paving), eye 1.5 to 1.9 m above the surface under it (1.7 to start), level (X rotation 90, Y 0). Turn ONCE so the roof and gallery lines meet beside the subject; after that only slide. A turn moves the subject and where the lines meet together; sliding does not. Plate lens 64.4 degrees against the film's 60.4, plate 1536 x 2730, painter returns 1504 x 2672.
- Story group: well, lamp, bucket and steps touching as one group, inside a box at most 0.40 of the frame wide and 0.50 tall; the nearest story thing reaches at least 0.70 down (the planner aims at 0.72), so the bottom third is story, not bare paving (a large courtyard makes that the main risk); nothing big and dark in the bottom-left quarter (1 percent of the frame at most); where the lines meet, the brightest parts, the warm light and the story props all fall in one part of the frame.
- Fill the height: top third roofline and bell turret with peaks above, middle the subject, bottom a soft near prop. A wide view is kind `overview` (a wider eye range; raise the eye, never tilt); the well close-up is `still_life`; a view with figures is `crowd`.
- Phone buttons: anything to read ends left of 0.90 across and above 0.80 down; story props left of 0.95; typed words sit in the band 0.05 to 0.22 down over dim sky or a soft dark band, so a tower top must be below 0.24 down (`view_audit.py` checks landmark tops).
- If figures appear: invented only, backs to the camera at 6 m or more from every spot along the slide, a small group two deep across the view, dark matt robes and hoods up (so the painter does not make a face), no long shadows. First test: none or at most two far figures, a story choice I ask about.
- Views (the planner proposes at least three; first one drawn): (1) wide from the gate to the hall steps and well; (2) eye-height well and worn cobbles; (3) hall door with lintel, iron and steps.

8. HOW I CHECK THE RESULT
- By tools, in this order: `construction` (every part carried, no float over 5 mm, spans 1.38 m or less, doorways with floors), the scale check (a 1.0 m door fails, 1.7 m passes), roles (fallback roles warn; over 15 percent fails), 17 treatments per role, normal maps Non-Color, tangent, 1024 px or more for a final, `normals-test`; displacement only on the nine roles that need it, normal strength times 0.6 there; "place: world", "place: sun", "place: film frame", "place: lettering", "place: budgets"; `measure` (value range, detail energy 0.9 to 1.4 times the guard and never above 10, flat windows, palette, squint 0.92 as a LOOK).
- By fresh helpers who did not build it: `place-checker` in modes look, structure, process and blind_reader (they never see the builders' reports or numbers; they recompute each claim with their own code; the blind reader sees half-size pictures only and must name at least 12 of 16 planned features, a judged line), then a skeptic that merges and ranks, exactly ONE fix round, then a DIFFERENT fresh checker and a second blind reader on the changed place. Final gate: `explainer-film-preflight place --place-audit ... --blend ... --place-pictures FOLDER --style-guard style-guard.json --fresh-check FRESH.json`.
- What only critics and the person can judge (tips guide section 19): does the wear read as designed rather than photographic; does a detail read as something else on a phone; are roofs, symbols, robes and inscriptions right for the tradition and period (history critic through `critique-film`; fact checker through `verify-facts` with `pictures` and `propLettering` from `list_prop_lettering.py`); whether a squint miss is acceptable. I report a miss with the region that loses most and never remove character to chase a number.
- Honest limits I will state: the plugin's tests prove the gates work, not that the place looks good; only a hut, a 36 x 26 m yard, small test scenes and a 12 m canal lock have been run (a courtyard of this size is near the top of what is tested, and Cycles with the kit at that size is not tested); the rented-card client has not been run against a real endpoint; the workflow and agents have not run under the real Workflow tool; the painter-route checks were tuned on EEVEE plates and not yet shown to hold for Cycles plates.

9. HOW I WORK WITH THE PERSON
- Start with what happened and what it means for their idea, in plain everyday words, one word for each thing; explain any technical word in a sentence first. Say what I tested, what I did not, and what I am unsure of; never say something works unless I ran it.
- Ask only about wants, risk or cost; make routine technical choices myself and list them so any can be overturned in one line. One next step, not a menu. When they are choosing a look, show a few versions of the SAME view where only the look changes (the `variations` sheet does this for free scouts and cheap batches), and say which I would pick and why.
